newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish president sees EMU starting on time.
newsitem.headline: Finnish president sees EMU starting on time.

text.p: Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari said on Thursday he expected the third phase of European economic and monetary union (EMU) to start on schedule at the beginning of 1999.
"I don't belong to those who think we are slipping from the first of January 1999 target, I think there is determination on that issue," he told a news conference.
Ahtisaari said he expected the issues still unresolved ahead of the European Union's summit meeting in Amsterdam next week to be settled and that EMU would stay on track.
"I don't read the political development in the member states in some such fashion that the (EMU) timetable is somehow in danger," he said.
"I am confident we will be working in Amsterdam -- and before Amsterdam -- towards resolution of the outstanding issues."

Ahtisaari was speaking a day after Finland lent support to France's demands that a treaty formula should be found to step up the European fight against unemployment and to coordinate economic policies of EU members once the single currency is in place.
Finland said it would support the introduction of a new text as an addition to the Maastrict treaty which envisages coordination of the EU member countries' economic policies.

It aims to be among the countries to launch EMU. Its views on EMU, including its backing for a strict interpretation of the qualifying criteria and its support for an independent central bank, have put it closer to Germany than to the Mediterranean EU members.

Ahtisaari said he hoped the stability pact, designed to enforce budgetary discipline in EMU, would be accepted and the EU should be able to harmonise economic policies within the existing articles of the Maastrict treaty.
"I hope the consultations that have been carried out in the last few days will provide something that is acceptable to all," he said.
